text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
--- Pressure from key clients has forced Danish banks to cut charges leading to still lower earnings in an industry where core earnings growth is a major problem.
--- Economy minister Marianne Jelved is to set up an independant board to control pension fund administration. Danish pension funds have a total holding of some 1,000 billion crowns.
--- Danish central bank governor Bodil Nyboe Andersen says there is no need at this stage for Denmark to tighten economic policies to curb inflation and shore up the current account surplus.

--- Sweden has become an important market for Danish cleaning group ISS' Care Service subsidiary with new orders to the tune of 54 million crowns for elderly care services. ISS Care Service hopes to use its experience with elderly care in Sweden to gain a foothold in other Scandinavian countries.
